panels.visual: The porch of the Erechtheion on the Acropolis: six marble maidens holding up the roof on their heads; a girl visitor looking up; one maiden winking
panels.caption: Look up. Six of us hold up the roof of this porch on our heads. We are the Caryatids.

panels.visual: Around 420 BC: a sculptor carving a marble maiden while a real girl poses with a jar balanced on her head
panels.caption: Sculptors carved us around 420 BC, like girls carrying offerings on their heads.

panels.visual: Close-up from behind of a Caryatid's head: a thick, beautifully carved plait down the back of her neck
panels.caption: Look at the backs of our heads: thick plaits. They make our necks strong enough to hold the roof.

panels.visual: The six sisters side by side, each face a little different, each with one knee bent as if about to step forward
panels.caption: Each of us is a little different. We bend one knee, as if we could walk away.

panels.visual: Around 1801: workmen in British coats sawing one Caryatid free and lowering her on ropes, the other sisters' stone eyes wide
panels.caption: Around 1801 Lord Elgin, a British ambassador, had his men take one sister away.

panels.visual: A sailing ship carrying a big wooden crate away to sea; on the porch, a plain brick pillar standing in her place
panels.caption: She was shipped to London. A brick pillar held up her corner.

panels.visual: Modern Athens traffic and grey fumes swirling round the porch, the marble faces getting grubby and pitted
panels.caption: Later, traffic fumes began to eat away our marble.

panels.visual: A crane gently lowering a padded Caryatid into a museum van while workers lift a copy into her place
panels.caption: So the five of us left were moved into the Acropolis Museum. The ones outside now are copies.

panels.visual: Inside the bright Acropolis Museum: five Caryatids standing together on a balcony gallery, with one empty space in the row
panels.caption: In the museum we stand together. The sixth place is empty.

panels.visual: A conservator in a mask gently cleaning a Caryatid's face with a thin laser beam, dirt lifting off
panels.caption: Cleaners use lasers to clean us, gently, one speck at a time.

panels.visual: A lonely Caryatid standing in a grand gallery of the British Museum in London, tourists walking past
panels.caption: Our sister is still in the British Museum in London.

panels.visual: Two girls and Glauka the owl standing in front of the empty space in the museum row, looking at it
panels.caption: Find the gap where she should stand. Greece has asked for her back for years.
